obligations.summary: Enumerate every recognized owner and competing command resolution before choosing an owner.
Require durable owner evidence; markers and paths alone cannot authorize destructive work.
obligations.oracle: ownership proof fixtures and adapter review

obligations.summary: Classify ownership as exactly one of absent, owned, degraded, conflict, unmanaged, or unknown.
Stop before mutation on conflicting, unmanaged, unknown, or unsafe ownership and report exact relevant evidence.
obligations.oracle: negative ownership fixtures and mutation journal

obligations.summary: Revalidate the complete ownership snapshot immediately before destructive mutation.
Resolve the latest release once and use exact-tag assets after resolution.
Verify product, version, target, size, digest, and every advertised native signature before mutation.
Treat published tags and assets as immutable and fix forward instead of overwriting bytes.
obligations.oracle: publication fixture and public asset audit

obligations.summary: Present existing installation, target, channel, scope, and data policy before destructive work.
obligations.oracle: terminal snapshots and install plan fixture

obligations.summary: Use private randomized staging, a lifecycle lock, and elevation before destructive operations.
A clean install commits exactly one owner and only required integrations.
Installing the same version through the same channel performs an idempotent repair.
Installing over an older recognized owner performs an approved takeover or stops safely; coexistence is forbidden.
Before mutation, establish a rollback plan that can restore the prior working installation or the absent state.
Commit only after one durable owner, one fresh-terminal resolution, the expected version, and no obsolete owner or backup remain.
obligations.oracle: post-install reconciliation fixture and installed-system probe

obligations.summary: Automatic update preserves the single proven install channel and never cross-falls back.
An already-current healthy install is a verified no-change result; a proven degraded owner may be repaired only through its channel.
Update verifies the installed executable version and durable owner before success.
Checksum, signature, installer, process-lock, elevation, policy, and restart outcomes use the shared failure vocabulary.
A failed update never claims success and verifies rollback when mutation began.
Interactive uninstall offers Remove All, Keep Data, and Cancel; JSON or non-TTY uninstall requires --yes.
Default confirmed uninstall removes the complete program, integrations, registrations, cache, logs, configuration, and app-owned state.
--keep-data removes the complete program and integrations while preserving declared application settings and state.
External exports, downloaded reports, host-owned data, and declared repository-local history are never removed.
Uninstall uses the exact proven package or owner mechanism and never selects the first similarly named registration.
Uninstall success requires verified absence of owners, payloads, registrations, integrations, backups, staging, and command resolution.
Post-exit self-removal is reported as pending_handoff until a constrained helper completes; spawning a helper is not success.
obligations.oracle: handoff fixture and helper completion receipt

obligations.summary: Uninstall against an absent installation is an idempotent not_installed result.
Family-owned headings, phases, symbols, warnings, failures, and summaries match the shared terminal snapshots.
JSON mode emits exactly one schema-valid object to stdout; diagnostics and child output never contaminate stdout.
Statuses, success, result, requires_user_action, restart_required, and process exit codes obey the shared mapping.
--no-color removes ANSI without changing content; --verbose adds diagnostics without changing semantic result or JSON shape.
Success is reported only after every mandatory postcondition is verified; pending work and residuals remain non-success.
Each adopter ADR pins the contract tag, commit, schema and fixture hashes, adapter, exceptions, sibling links, and evidence.
Products have no runtime, build, release, installer, updater, uninstaller, Git, or network dependency on this repository.
Every exception is explicit, approved, tested, and unable to waive core destructive-safety and truthfulness invariants.
Simulated fixtures and source tests do not substitute for installed-package qualification on advertised targets.
The completion receipt records every mandatory case, oracle, evidence pointer, limitation, and truthful status.
